privacy.note: This public demo contains deterministic fictional measurements and no personal health records.

daily_health.title: Synthetic daily health signals
daily_health.description: One fictional row per calendar day across sleep, recovery, oxygen, temperature and activity.

source.label: Deterministic synthetic demo generator
caveats: Every measurement belongs to a fictional demo profile; no personal health record was used as an input.
Values are plausible simulations for product demonstration and must not be used for medical decisions.
Missing values are intentional and remain null rather than being converted to zero.

daily_health.method: Generate deterministic daily signals with bounded noise, gradual fitness trends, weekend effects, cross-metric relationships and explicit missing sleep nights.

evidenceFlow.title: Synthetic generation
evidenceFlow.detail: A deterministic sequence models a gradual 1.5 kg change across six fictional measurements; height remains fixed at 1.72 m.

recommendation_evidence.title: Evidence-linked recommendations for a fictional profile
recommendation_evidence.description: Educational recommendations generated from the synthetic workout mix, fictional weight and demo location.

source.label: Deterministic synthetic demo generator
caveats: Recommendations describe a fictional profile and are present only to demonstrate dashboard behavior.
Wearable signals cannot diagnose vitamin, mineral or hormone deficiency.
The interface is educational and does not replace a clinician, pharmacist or registered dietitian.

recommendation_evidence.method: Count fictional workout types, calculate a protein reference from fictional weight, illustrate location-dependent vitamin D guidance and withhold unsupported deficiency treatment.

rows.personalBasis: 18 of 36 fictional workouts are resistance-training sessions.
rows.dose: 3–5 g/day is shown as an educational reference for a healthy fictional adult.
rows.evidence: Sports-nutrition evidence supports creatine for repeated high-intensity exercise.
rows.limitation: The synthetic wearable signals do not establish a deficiency or individual response.
rows.caution: Medical context is intentionally absent from the demo profile.
rows.sourceTitle: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements — Exercise and Athletic Performance

rows.personalBasis: The fictional profile combines resistance training with a latest weight of 70.9 kg.
rows.dose: A 1.6 g/kg/day reference corresponds to about 113 g/day, pending a dietary audit.
rows.evidence: A meta-analysis found limited additional lean-mass benefit above roughly 1.6 g/kg/day.
rows.limitation: No fictional food diary is included, so a dietary gap is not established.
rows.sourceTitle: Morton et al. — systematic review and meta-analysis

rows.personalBasis: The demo uses Europe/Dublin to illustrate a location-dependent recommendation.
rows.dose: The interface shows current HSE population guidance, not an inferred deficiency.
rows.evidence: HSE publishes seasonal vitamin D guidance for Ireland.
rows.limitation: Wearables do not measure vitamin D status.
rows.caution: Treatment dosing would require clinical context and, when indicated, testing.
rows.sourceTitle: Health Service Executive Ireland — Vitamin D

rows.personalBasis: The fictional sleep and HRV trends do not identify a nutrient deficiency.
rows.dose: No routine dose is generated for magnesium, iron, B12 or melatonin.
rows.evidence: The dashboard demonstrates a conservative evidence boundary.
rows.limitation: Diet, symptoms, medicines and laboratory results are absent.
rows.caution: A real user should discuss persistent symptoms with a qualified professional.
rows.sourceTitle: Lopresti et al. — systematic review of magnesium RCTs
